record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: Suppose every arriving job has a hard deadline of 400 ms and the objective is to minimize the fraction of jobs whose response time exceeds that deadline. What scheduling policy minimizes P{Response time > 400 ms}?

evidence.quote: How to schedule jobs to minimize P {Response time > 400 ms} is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an M/G/1 queue: jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$, and the service times (job sizes) are i.i.d. with a known general distribution $S$, independent of the arrival process, with $\rho = \lambda \mathbb{E}[S] < 1$. The server processes work at unit rate, and a scheduling policy is a (possibly preemptive, size-based) rule that, at each time, selects which job in the system to serve. The response time $T$ of a job is the time from its arrival until its completion.

Fix a deadline $d = 400$ ms (in the units of service time). Among all work-conserving scheduling policies that may use full knowledge of job sizes and arrival times, determine the policy $\pi^\star$ that minimizes the steady-state probability
$$\mathbb{P}\{T > d\}$$
that a job's response time exceeds the deadline $d$. Equivalently, find the scheduling discipline that minimizes the fraction of jobs whose response time exceeds $400$ ms, and characterize the optimal value.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding a scheduling policy that minimizes the tail probability P{Response time > d} for a fixed deadline d in an M/G/1-type queue is listed as an open problem in the queueing-theory open-problems survey on datacenter computing. While SRPT is known to minimize mean response time in M/G/1 (Schrage 1968), no policy is known to minimize the deadline-miss probability for a fixed finite deadline, and the relevant literature continues to treat this as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
status_evidence.snippet: Suggestions for specific open problems including how to schedule to minimize the deadline-miss probability.
status_evidence.claim: The deadline-miss minimization scheduling problem is posed as an open problem in this survey of queueing open problems.

status_evidence.title: M/G/1 Model with 4 Categories of Scheduling Policies
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of M/G/1 scheduling policies and their response-time properties; SRPT minimizes mean response time but tail-optimal policy is not known.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on M/G/1 scheduling do not provide a policy known to minimize P{T > d} for a fixed deadline d.
